title: 05. Retrieval, Hybrid & Reranking: Metadata Filtering (Native)
summary: Metadata Filtering (Native): explanations and runnable examples.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```python name=00_theory/03_metadata_filtering_native.py
"""
CHAPTER 3: Metadata Filtering in ChromaDB (Native)

ChromaDB supports TWO filter types:
  1. `where`          → filter on METADATA fields
  2. `where_document` → filter on DOCUMENT TEXT content

Both use operator syntax: {"field": {"$op": value}}

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
WHERE OPERATORS (metadata)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Comparison:  $eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte
Membership:  $in, $nin
Logical:     $and, $or

WHERE_DOCUMENT OPERATORS (document text)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  $contains     → text contains substring
  $not_contains → text does NOT contain substring
"""

import chromadb

client = chromadb.Client()
col = client.get_or_create_collection(
    name="articles",
    metadata={"hnsw:space": "cosine"},
)

# ── Seed data ──────────────────────────────────────
col.add(
    ids=[f"doc-{i}" for i in range(1, 13)],
    documents=[
        "Machine learning enables computers to learn from data automatically.",
        "Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers.",
        "Natural language processing helps computers understand human language.",
        "Computer vision allows machines to interpret images.",
        "Reinforcement learning trains agents through rewards and penalties.",
        "Python is the most popular language for data science.",
        "TensorFlow and PyTorch are leading deep learning frameworks.",
        "Transformers revolutionized NLP with self-attention mechanisms.",
        "GPT-4 is a large language model developed by OpenAI.",
        "Stable Diffusion generates images from text descriptions.",
        "Data preprocessing is a critical step in machine learning pipelines.",
        "Model evaluation metrics include accuracy, precision, and recall.",
    ],
    metadatas=[
        {"category": "ml",       "author": "alice",   "year": 2023, "level": "beginner",     "rating": 4.5},
        {"category": "dl",       "author": "bob",     "year": 2022, "level": "intermediate",  "rating": 4.2},
        {"category": "nlp",      "author": "alice",   "year": 2023, "level": "beginner",     "rating": 4.8},
        {"category": "cv",       "author": "charlie", "year": 2022, "level": "intermediate",  "rating": 3.9},
        {"category": "rl",       "author": "bob",     "year": 2021, "level": "advanced",     "rating": 4.1},
        {"category": "tools",    "author": "alice",   "year": 2023, "level": "beginner",     "rating": 4.6},
        {"category": "dl",       "author": "charlie", "year": 2023, "level": "intermediate",  "rating": 4.3},
        {"category": "nlp",      "author": "bob",     "year": 2023, "level": "advanced",     "rating": 4.7},
        {"category": "llm",      "author": "alice",   "year": 2023, "level": "intermediate",  "rating": 4.9},
        {"category": "cv",       "author": "charlie", "year": 2023, "level": "advanced",     "rating": 4.4},
        {"category": "ml",       "author": "bob",     "year": 2022, "level": "beginner",     "rating": 4.0},
        {"category": "ml",       "author": "alice",   "year": 2022, "level": "intermediate",  "rating": 3.8},
    ],
)
print(f"✅ Seeded {col.count()} documents\n")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 1: Simple Equality Filter
# ════════════════════════════════════════════
print("=" * 55)
print("EXAMPLE 1: Simple equality filter")
print("=" * 55)

# 1a. Filter by category
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["tell me about neural networks"],
    n_results=3,
    where={"category": {"$eq": "dl"}},           # $eq is same as just {"category": "dl"}
    include=["documents", "metadatas", "distances"],
)
print("\n[1a] where category == 'dl':")
for doc, meta, dist in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0], results["distances"][0]):
    print(f"  dist={dist:.3f} | {doc[:60]} | author={meta['author']}")

# 1b. Filter by author
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["machine learning basics"],
    n_results=5,
    where={"author": {"$eq": "alice"}},
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[1b] where author == 'alice':")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  {doc[:60]} | cat={meta['category']}")

# 1c. Filter by level using shorthand (no operator needed for $eq)
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["advanced techniques"],
    n_results=3,
    where={"level": "advanced"},           # shorthand for $eq
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[1c] where level == 'advanced' (shorthand):")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  {doc[:60]} | author={meta['author']}")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 2: Comparison & Membership Filters
# ════════════════════════════════════════════
print("\n" + "=" * 55)
print("EXAMPLE 2: Comparison & Membership Filters")
print("=" * 55)

# 2a. Numeric comparison: year >= 2023
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["latest AI research"],
    n_results=4,
    where={"year": {"$gte": 2023}},
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[2a] where year >= 2023:")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  year={meta['year']} | {doc[:60]}")

# 2b. Rating above threshold
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["best articles"],
    n_results=4,
    where={"rating": {"$gt": 4.5}},
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[2b] where rating > 4.5:")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  rating={meta['rating']} | {doc[:60]}")

# 2c. $in operator — category in list
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["language understanding"],
    n_results=4,
    where={"category": {"$in": ["nlp", "llm"]}},
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[2c] where category in ['nlp', 'llm']:")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  cat={meta['category']} | {doc[:60]}")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 3: Logical Operators ($and, $or)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════
print("\n" + "=" * 55)
print("EXAMPLE 3: Logical Operators")
print("=" * 55)

# 3a. $and — multiple conditions must ALL be true
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["learning techniques"],
    n_results=3,
    where={
        "$and": [
            {"author": {"$eq": "alice"}},
            {"year": {"$gte": 2023}},
        ]
    },
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[3a] where author=='alice' AND year>=2023:")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  {doc[:60]} | year={meta['year']}")

# 3b. $or — at least ONE condition must be true
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["image and language AI"],
    n_results=4,
    where={
        "$or": [
            {"category": {"$eq": "cv"}},
            {"category": {"$eq": "nlp"}},
        ]
    },
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[3b] where category=='cv' OR category=='nlp':")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  cat={meta['category']} | {doc[:60]}")

# 3c. Nested $and + $or
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["AI research 2023"],
    n_results=3,
    where={
        "$and": [
            {"year": {"$gte": 2023}},
            {
                "$or": [
                    {"level": {"$eq": "advanced"}},
                    {"rating": {"$gte": 4.7}},
                ]
            },
        ]
    },
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[3c] where year>=2023 AND (level=='advanced' OR rating>=4.7):")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  {meta['level']} | rating={meta['rating']} | {doc[:55]}")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 4: where_document (text filtering)
# ════════════════════════════════════════════
print("\n" + "=" * 55)
print("EXAMPLE 4: where_document — text content filters")
print("=" * 55)

# 4a. Document contains a word
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["AI learning"],
    n_results=3,
    where_document={"$contains": "neural"},
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[4a] where_document contains 'neural':")
for doc in results["documents"][0]:
    print(f"  {doc}")

# 4b. Document does NOT contain a word
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["machine learning"],
    n_results=3,
    where_document={"$not_contains": "language"},
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[4b] where_document NOT contains 'language':")
for doc in results["documents"][0]:
    print(f"  {doc}")

# 4c. Combine where + where_document
results = col.query(
    query_texts=["deep learning models"],
    n_results=3,
    where={"year": {"$gte": 2023}},
    where_document={"$contains": "learning"},
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print("\n[4c] year>=2023 AND document contains 'learning':")
for doc, meta in zip(results["documents"][0], results["metadatas"][0]):
    print(f"  year={meta['year']} | {doc[:60]}")

# ════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXAMPLE 5: col.get() with filters
# ════════════════════════════════════════════
print("\n" + "=" * 55)
print("EXAMPLE 5: col.get() with where filter (no query)")
print("=" * 55)

# Get ALL docs by author (no similarity search, pure filter)
fetched = col.get(
    where={"author": {"$eq": "bob"}},
    include=["documents", "metadatas"],
)
print(f"\n[5] All docs by author='bob' ({len(fetched['documents'])} found):")
for doc, meta in zip(fetched["documents"], fetched["metadatas"]):
    print(f"  cat={meta['category']} | {doc[:60]}")
```
